patches.reason: The viewer combines independently-authored CDE files into one classic global script. Preserving top-level const/let/class declarations gives that generated script temporal-dead-zone and duplicate-lexical-binding behavior that does not belong to the CDE flattened-global contract. It is also the underlying reason project boot functions such as IrancellCoreStoreV2InitLogic can fail depending on browser/runtime ordering. Normalize only the flattened top level to classic var-style globals and separate executable top-level statements so project boot code can be delayed until definitions from every CDE source are ready.

After imports and exports have been normalized, capture top-level execution statements separately from declarations. This makes calls, IIFEs, event registration, boot logic, and other global execution run only after all CDE implementation files have established their shared declarations. The generated declaration code remains in the normal flattened scope, so existing CDE global symbol semantics are preserved.

The old merger executed every file completely as soon as it was concatenated and only recovered exports at the very end. That means a Core file can call its initializer before another Core declaration or shared repository symbol has initialized. Build the output in three deterministic phases instead: declarations/initializers, export recovery, then deferred top-level execution. Also track both normal and deferred source ranges correctly for diagnostics.

The compiler currently explicitly targets Chrome 100, so its generated output is allowed to contain syntax and transformations selected only for Chromium. That contradicts the viewer requirement to execute the same compiled CDE on Firefox, desktop Safari, and iOS Safari. Compile against a conservative shared browser baseline instead.

Safari/iOS Safari and Firefox can restrict localStorage or sessionStorage for sandboxed/srcdoc documents, private browsing, or other privacy contexts. The current compatibility store evaluates global.localStorage before entering readStorage's try block, so the browser can throw before the fallback has a chance to run. Resolve browser storage defensively and make persistence optional rather than allowing a CDE project to fail during store initialization.

Persistence currently re-reads global.localStorage/global.sessionStorage each time and can throw on browsers that expose the property but deny access. Reuse the safely resolved storage handles and silently operate as an in-memory store when persistent browser storage is unavailable.

Add compiler-level regression coverage for the actual architecture bug: a CDE file may contain an eager top-level boot call that uses a declaration supplied by another flattened file, and multiple independently parsed files may use the same top-level lexical alias. These tests ensure future fixes remain generic and do not regress into project-specific patches.

The remaining stack ends at IrancellCoreStoreV2BuildModels -> global code, which means model construction is still executing eagerly while the flattened CDE script is evaluating. Even though the boot seed is declared earlier in the original source, flattened CDE execution can expose initialization-order hazards. Keep one stable models array for exported references, populate it lazily after IrancellCoreStoreV2State is initialized, and use that initialized state as the model seed.
The underlying data-store must trigger lazy model creation when it is actually ready rather than consuming the previously eager global model result.
getModel must also work before or without successful underlying createStore initialization. Ensure the stable exported model array has been populated before searching it.

The runtime stack fails while IrancellCoreStoreV2BuildModels calls IrancellCoreStoreV2ReadPublishedSeed during global script initialization. The published/local seed has already been completely resolved into IRANCELL_CORE_STORE_V2_BOOT_SEED before store state and models are created, so re-evaluating LOCAL_STORE_MODE and LOCAL_SEED during global initialization is unnecessary and can hit lexical initialization ordering in the flattened CDE runtime. Read from the already-normalized boot seed instead while retaining the safe seed as a defensive fallback.

Model definitions are created at top-level while the flattened CDE script is booting. They must use the already-resolved boot seed directly instead of invoking a runtime seed resolver during global evaluation. This removes the IrancellCoreStoreV2ReadPublishedSeed -> IrancellCoreStoreV2BuildModels -> global code failure path while preserving the same fixture/remote seed selected earlier by IRANCELL_CORE_STORE_V2_BOOT_SEED.
